patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma on pembrolizumab at an outside oncology group, severe COPD on 2 L home oxygen, type 2 diabetes with nephropathy, CKD 3b, PAD after a left fem-pop bypass and hypertension. Two septic shock admissions (2024 pneumonia with an iatrogenic pneumothorax from a subclavian line; 2026 with no source and AKI). Married; his wife is his proxy.

Release signed by pt at the window this afternoon for records from the prior primary care office and from his oncology group. Both requests sent.

Summary letter from that office: Mr. Coolidge was followed there for COPD on continuous home oxygen at 2 L, type 2 diabetes with diabetic kidney disease, chronic kidney disease stage 3b, hypertension and peripheral arterial disease. Left femoral-popliteal bypass with a synthetic graft in 2019. Diagnostic cardiac catheterization in 2018; the report is not in the packet. In May 2023 a left upper lobe mass was biopsied under CT guidance and mediastinoscopy was done; adenocarcinoma, now under an outside oncology group. Quit smoking at that time after about 50 pack-years.

Screening: colonoscopy 2018, no polyps.

Medications at last visit: albuterol-ipratropium inhaler as needed, metformin 500 mg twice daily, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, oxycodone 5 mg as needed (oncology), home oxygen.

Also enclosed: spirometry from March 2022, filed as a result.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
64M here with his wife to establish care. Prior PCP records reviewed (packet received 8/14).

HPI: Diagnosed in May with a left upper lobe adenocarcinoma, stage IV per his oncologist, after a CT-guided biopsy and a mediastinoscopy. Started immunotherapy infusions in June, every three weeks, and is tolerating them; some tiredness for a day or two after each. Oncology manages his pain prescription; he takes the oxycodone maybe once a day, sometimes not at all. Breathing is his usual: on 2 L around the clock, uses the Combivent a few times a week when he exerts. Diabetes on metformin alone, says sugars were fine at the last office. Kidney numbers have been reduced for years. Left leg bypass in 2019, no leg pain walking around the house now.

PMH: as above plus hypertension. Heart cath in 2018, says he was told nothing needed fixing; no report available.
PSH: L fem-pop bypass 2019 (synthetic graft); CT-guided LUL core biopsy and mediastinoscopy 5/2023.
Meds: Combivent 2 puffs q6h prn; metformin 500 mg BID with meals; ASA 81; atorvastatin 40; amlodipine 5; oxycodone IR 5 mg q6h prn (oncology); pembrolizumab q3 weeks (oncology); home O2 2 L/min continuous.
Allergies: sulfa antibiotics (hives); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis, needs premedication if ever unavoidable).
FH: father lung cancer, died at 67, smoked heavily. Mother living, 87, type 2 diabetes and CKD. Older brother MI at 62.
SH: married, lives with wife in Amherst. Retired construction foreman. Smoked about 50 pack-years, stopped in May at the diagnosis. A beer or two a week. Wife drives him to appointments.

ROS: no fever, no chest pain, no hemoptysis, no leg ulcers, no urinary complaints. PHQ-2 0.

Exam: thin, pleasant, on nasal cannula, speaks in full sentences. Vitals as charted. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs: air movement decreased throughout, no wheeze, no crackles. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext: well-healed left thigh and knee incisions, feet warm, pedal pulses present, no ulcers, monofilament sensation intact both feet. Neuro grossly intact.

Assessment and plan:
1. Stage IV LUL adenocarcinoma on pembrolizumab: oncology leads; requested their notes and pathology.
2. Severe COPD on continuous O2: continue Combivent prn and oxygen. PCV20 today.
3. T2DM with nephropathy, CKD 3b: metformin at current dose is appropriate for his kidney function. A1c, CMP, UACR today.
4. HTN: 134/78 on amlodipine 5, fine.
5. PAD s/p bypass: aspirin and atorvastatin, lipid panel today.
6. One-time hepatitis C and HIV screening, agreed.
7. Flu, COVID and RSV vaccines in early October at a nurse visit.

RTC about 3-4 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Coolidge, your labs from yesterday are back. Kidney function is reduced, about where your old office had it, and the urine protein is elevated as expected with diabetic kidney disease. A1c is in a reasonable range for you. Cholesterol on the atorvastatin looks good. Blood counts are normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. No changes for now. We'll recheck in December.

reports.text: Specimen: lung, left upper lobe, CT-guided core needle biopsy, four cores. Microscopic: invasive adenocarcinoma. Immunohistochemistry supports a lung primary. Tissue sent for molecular testing and PD-L1 staining (reported separately).
reports.conclusion: Left upper lobe, core biopsy: invasive adenocarcinoma, lung primary.

documents.title: Medical oncology consultation (outside)
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology. Date of consultation: 06/05/2023. Received 9/6/2023 at PCP request.

Reason: newly diagnosed lung adenocarcinoma.

64-year-old retired foreman, 50 pack-year smoker who stopped last month, with severe COPD on continuous oxygen, diabetes, stage 3b CKD and PAD. Left upper lobe mass biopsied 5/11 under CT guidance, invasive adenocarcinoma; mediastinoscopy with nodal sampling performed. Staging complete: stage IV disease.

Biomarkers: next-generation sequencing shows no actionable driver alteration. PD-L1 tumor proportion score 60%.

Allergies: sulfa antibiotics (hives); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis). Imaging here will be done without IV contrast.

Plan: single-agent pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks, first dose planned this month. Platinum doublet not favored given kidney function and pulmonary reserve. Restaging CT chest without contrast every 3 cycles or so. Oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed for cancer-related pain, prescribed through this office. Immunotherapy side effects reviewed with the patient and his wife.

documents.title: Nurse visit: vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In with wife for fall vaccines. Checked with oncology infusion schedule: last pembrolizumab dose 9/26, no conflict. Screening questions negative. High-dose flu L deltoid, updated Moderna COVID R deltoid, RSV L deltoid lower site. VIS sheets given. Observed 15 minutes on his own oxygen, no reaction. Told to expect a sore arm and maybe a tired day.

reports.text: CT chest without IV contrast (contrast allergy). Comparison: staging study, May 2023. Left upper lobe mass measures 2.8 cm, not significantly changed. No new pulmonary nodules. No pleural effusion. Heart size normal. No acute findings in the imaged upper abdomen.
reports.conclusion: Stable left upper lobe mass, 2.8 cm. No new lesions.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology. Visit 10/19/2023.

Dear colleague, Mr. Coolidge has had five cycles of pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks. Tolerating it with mild fatigue. No rash, no diarrhea, no new cough. Restaging CT chest without contrast 10/17 shows the left upper lobe mass stable at 2.8 cm with no new lesions: stable disease. We will continue the same treatment and repeat imaging in about three months. Oxycodone continues as needed, using little. Allergies on file: sulfa antibiotics, iodinated contrast.

Feels about the same. Breathing at baseline on 2 L, using the rescue inhaler a couple of times a week. Appetite fair. No hypoglycemia symptoms, doesn't check sugars at home. No foot sores. Oxycodone rarely, per oncology.

Exam: comfortable on cannula. Vitals as charted. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs with reduced air entry, no wheeze. No ankle swelling. Feet intact, no ulcers.

A/P:
- DM2 with nephropathy: on metformin 500 BID, A1c and BMP today.
- CKD 3b: BMP today, avoid NSAIDs (reminded him).
- HTN: at goal on amlodipine.
- COPD on O2, lung cancer: per oncology.
RTC 3 months.

Quarterly visit. Wife with him. February oncology letter in the chart: stable on CT, still on pembrolizumab.

Winter was quiet. No hospital trips. Stays inside on cold days, walks the hallway at home. Oxygen 2 L continuous. Rescue inhaler two or three times a week. Eating okay. No dizziness.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial AWV. Wife present.

Health risk review: independent with dressing, bathing, meals; wife handles driving and most errands. No falls this year; uses a cart for the oxygen tank and holds the rail on stairs. Hearing and vision adequate, glasses for reading. PHQ-9 3. AUDIT-C 1. Former smoker, quit 5/2023.

Current providers: outside oncology (pembrolizumab q3 wk), oxygen supplier, optometrist due this summer.

Advance care planning, about 25 minutes with patient and wife: he understands the cancer is not curable and that treatment is aimed at control. For now he wants full treatment including hospital and ICU care if needed. Names his wife as health care proxy; form completed and scanned. Will revisit if things change.

Exam: vitals as charted. Heart RRR. Lungs diminished bilaterally, no wheeze. No edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament normal, pedal pulses present.

Screening: colonoscopy 2018 normal, not repeating. Lung screening not applicable. Vaccines: PCV20, RSV, Shingrix x2 done; flu and COVID due this fall.

Labs: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine albumin/creatinine.

Plan: personalized prevention schedule given. Diabetic eye exam reminder. Follow-up in September.

documents.title: Emergency department record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, date of service 11/15/2024. Copy received 11/18/2024.

CC: confused and not eating or drinking since yesterday.

HPI: 65-year-old man with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma on immunotherapy, severe COPD on 2 L home oxygen, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3b and PAD, brought in by his wife. Per wife, his cough has been getting worse and more productive over several days, and this morning he could barely walk. No travel, no known sick contacts.

Home meds: Combivent prn, metformin 500 mg BID, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, amlodipine 5, oxycodone 5 mg prn, home O2 2 L.
Allergies: sulfa antibiotics (hives); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).
Former smoker, 50 pack-years, quit May 2023. Retired foreman.

Triage: temp 35.5 C, HR 122, RR 26, BP 84/52, SpO2 90% on room air.

Exam: confused, does not know where he is or the date. Mucous membranes dry. Diminished breath sounds over the right lower lung field, crackles at both bases. Heart sounds normal, no JVD. No peripheral edema. Skin without rash; no signs of trauma.

Data: WBC 23.0 with 14% bands. Lactate 4.5. BUN 28, creatinine 2.1, glucose 148. ABG on room air: pH 7.30, PaCO2 32, HCO3 15. Portable chest film: large right lower lobe consolidation with air bronchograms.

Assessment: septic shock due to right lower lobe pneumonia, with lactic acidosis.

ED course: blood cultures drawn, IV fluid boluses, vancomycin and cefepime given (sulfa allergy noted). Pressure remained soft after fluids. ICU consulted and accepted; admitted to the ICU.

conditions.label: Postprocedural pneumothorax
conditions.note: Simple right pneumothorax after right subclavian central line

reports.text: Stat portable AP chest after right subclavian central venous catheter placement. The catheter tip projects over the right apex, outside the expected course of the superior vena cava. Right pneumothorax. Right lower lobe consolidation as before.
reports.conclusion: Malpositioned right subclavian catheter with right pneumothorax.

reports.text: Portable AP chest after right chest tube placement and new right internal jugular catheter. Chest tube in the right hemithorax. Right lung re-expanded; no residual pneumothorax. Internal jugular catheter tip in the superior vena cava. Subclavian catheter removed. Right lower lobe consolidation unchanged.
reports.conclusion: Right lung re-expanded. Line tip in SVC.

documents.title: ICU event note (outside)
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Outside ICU, event note dated 11/15/2024. Received with the discharge summary 11/26/2024.

65M admitted from the ED today in septic shock from right lower lobe pneumonia, background of stage IV lung adenocarcinoma, severe COPD on home O2 and CKD 3b. On vancomycin and cefepime. Right subclavian central line placed for norepinephrine; no immediate problems. MAP improved with fluids and pressor.

About half an hour after the line went in he became acutely short of breath with chest pain; saturation fell to 88% on room air. BP 85/50, HR 120, T 38.9. Breath sounds diminished on the right; trachea shifted to the left. Stat film: catheter tip over the right apex outside the SVC shadow, right pneumothorax.

Labs this afternoon: Hgb 12.2, WBC 18.0, platelets 250, Na 138, K 4.2, BUN 28.

Action: right chest tube placed at the bedside; subclavian catheter removed and a right internal jugular line placed under ultrasound. Repeat film: lung re-expanded, IJ tip in SVC. Oxygenation back to his baseline on nasal cannula. Wife updated at the bedside.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (outside)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 11/15/2024, discharged 11/25/2024.

Diagnoses: septic shock due to right lower lobe pneumonia; lactic acidosis; leukocytosis; iatrogenic simple right pneumothorax after subclavian line placement, treated with chest tube.
Chronic: stage IV lung adenocarcinoma on pembrolizumab; severe COPD on home oxygen 2 L; type 2 diabetes with nephropathy; CKD 3b; PAD after left fem-pop bypass; hypertension.

Course: ICU from the ED. Vancomycin and cefepime for the pneumonia, completed in hospital. Norepinephrine off by hospital day 3. Pneumothorax after the subclavian line was managed with a right chest tube; lung stayed expanded and the tube came out on day 4. Mental status back to normal by day 3. Transferred to the floor day 5, worked with PT, walking the hall on his usual 2 L at discharge. Creatinine stayed near his known baseline. Metformin and amlodipine held during the stay and resumed at discharge. Pembrolizumab on hold until his oncologist sees him.

Discharge medications: Combivent prn, metformin 500 mg BID, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, oxycodone 5 mg prn, home oxygen 2 L/min continuous. No antibiotics at discharge.

Allergies: sulfa antibiotics (hives); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; oncology in 2 to 3 weeks.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with pt and wife, home since yesterday afternoon. Discharge summary received and reviewed. Tired but eating and drinking. No fever. Breathing at his usual on 2 L. Chest tube site dry, dressing off. Med list reviewed against discharge list, no changes; he has all meds at home. Knows to call or come in for fever, confusion or worse breathing. Post-hospital visit booked Mon 12/2.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen one week after discharge. ED record, ICU event note and discharge summary all reviewed.

Summary: 11/15-11/25 ICU admission for septic shock from RLL pneumonia with lactic acidosis; course complicated by a right pneumothorax from the subclavian line, chest tube, resolved. Off pressors day 3, antibiotics finished inpatient.

Today: says he is "about 80 percent." Thinking clearly, per wife back to himself. Cough much less. No fever. Walking the house on 2 L. Eating better. Oncology visit on the 10th to talk about restarting pembrolizumab.

Exam: alert, oriented, on cannula. Vitals as charted. Right chest tube site healed, clean. Right IJ and subclavian sites clean. Heart regular. Lungs: diminished overall, no crackles. No edema.

A/P:
- Septic shock, RLL pneumonia, lactic acidosis: resolved clinically. CBC today.
- Iatrogenic pneumothorax: resolved.
- CKD 3b: BMP today to confirm he is back to baseline.
- DM2: metformin resumed at discharge, continue.
- Meds reconciled with discharge list, no changes.
- Oncology to follow up imaging; their next CT should show the consolidation clearing.
RTC March, sooner for any fever or confusion.

reports.text: CT chest without IV contrast. Comparison 6/18/2024 and outside chest radiographs from November 2024. The right lower lobe consolidation seen on the November films has resolved. No pneumothorax. Left upper lobe mass 2.8 cm, unchanged. No new nodules. No effusion.
reports.conclusion: Resolved right lower lobe consolidation. Stable left upper lobe mass. No new disease.

reports.text: Portable AP chest after right internal jugular central venous catheter placement. Catheter tip at the cavoatrial junction. No pneumothorax. No focal consolidation. No pleural effusion. Known left upper lobe mass is better assessed on CT.
reports.conclusion: Line in good position. No pneumothorax or consolidation.

documents.title: Emergency department record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 5/19/2026; copy received 5/21/2026.

CC: two days of fever, shaking chills and confusion.

HPI: 67-year-old man with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma off immunotherapy since mid-2025, severe COPD on continuous 2 L oxygen, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3b and PAD after a left fem-pop bypass in 2019. His wife says he hasn't been acting like himself, sleepy and mixed up. Previously admitted here in November 2024, eighteen months ago, with septic shock and a line-associated pneumothorax.

Meds: Combivent prn, metformin 500 BID, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, amlodipine 5, oxycodone 5 prn, O2 2 L.
Allergies: sulfa antibiotics (hives); iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).
Former smoker, 50 pack-years, quit 2023.

Vitals on arrival: T 39.2 C, BP 85/50, HR 120, RR 22.

Exam: drowsy, disoriented. Skin warm and flushed; capillary refill less than 2 seconds.

Labs: WBC 18.0, Hgb 12.0, platelets 150. Creatinine 2.5 (baseline 1.9), BUN 40. Lactate 4.5. ABG pH 7.30, PaCO2 32, HCO3 18.

Procedure: right internal jugular central venous catheter under ultrasound guidance. Hemodynamics: cardiac index 4.2 L/min/m2, SVR 700 dyn-s/cm5, mixed venous O2 saturation 75%, a distributive picture.

Assessment: septic shock, source not yet clear; acute kidney injury on CKD; lactic acidosis.

Plan: blood and urine cultures, broad-spectrum antibiotics started (vancomycin and cefepime), fluids, norepinephrine. Admit ICU.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (outside)
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted 5/19/2026 via the ED; discharged 5/27/2026.

Principal: septic shock, source not identified.
Secondary: acute kidney injury on CKD 3b; lactic acidosis; leukocytosis.
Chronic: stage IV lung adenocarcinoma under surveillance; severe COPD on home O2 2 L; type 2 diabetes with nephropathy; CKD 3b; PAD after left fem-pop bypass; hypertension.

Hospital course: ICU for two days on norepinephrine, then weaned and moved to the medical floor. Blood and urine cultures without growth; chest film without consolidation. No source found despite a careful search. Vancomycin and cefepime for 7 days, completed here. Lactate cleared within 24 hours. Creatinine peaked at admission and was 2.0 on the day of discharge. Confusion resolved by day 2. Metformin and amlodipine held in hospital; resumed at discharge with creatinine near baseline. Central line removed before discharge.

Discharge medications: Combivent prn, metformin 500 mg BID, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, oxycodone 5 mg prn, home O2 2 L continuous. No antibiotics at discharge.

Allergies: sulfa antibiotics (hives), iodinated contrast (anaphylaxis).

Follow-up: PCP within one week with a BMP; oncology as scheduled.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called the home; spoke with pt, wife on speaker. Discharged yesterday after the septic shock admission (summary in chart this morning). No fever overnight. Eating small meals, drinking. Thinking clearly. Tired, resting a lot. Meds match the discharge list; metformin and amlodipine back on. Line site on the neck clean. Visit set for Wed 6/3 with labs. Return precautions reviewed.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. ED record and discharge summary reviewed.

Admitted 5/19-5/27 with septic shock, no source found, cultures negative, CXR clear. AKI on CKD (Cr 2.5 vs baseline 1.9), lactic acidosis. Pressors 2 days, 7 days of vanc/cefepime. Discharge Cr 2.0.

Today: no fever since discharge. Mind clear. Tires more easily than before. Eating, drinking more than usual at wife's insistence. Breathing at his baseline on 2 L.

Exam: alert, oriented x3. Vitals as charted. Neck line site healed. Heart regular. Lungs diminished, no crackles. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin warm, no rash.

A/P:
- Septic shock, lactic acidosis: resolved.
- AKI on CKD 3b: improving, Cr 2.0 at discharge; BMP today. Leave AKI on the list until creatinine is back at baseline. Continue metformin at 500 BID with eGFR above 30. No NSAIDs.
- DM2, HTN: meds unchanged.
RTC 7/20 as planned, sooner with any fever.

reports.text: CT chest without contrast. Comparison 2/3/2026. Left upper lobe mass 2.8 cm, unchanged. No new nodules. No consolidation or effusion. No pneumothorax.

documents.title: Oncology surveillance letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body: Outside medical oncology, visit 6/11/2026. Seen after his May admission for septic shock without a source. Recovering. Surveillance CT 6/9 unchanged, mass 2.8 cm, no new disease, nothing to suggest the cancer played a part. Continuing surveillance; next CT in about four months. Allergies: sulfa antibiotics, iodinated contrast.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after the May admission. June oncology letter: surveillance CT stable.

Feels like himself again. Energy back to his usual. No fevers. Breathing baseline on 2 L, rescue inhaler a few times a week. No lightheadedness on amlodipine.

Exam: vitals as charted. NAD. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs with diminished air entry, no wheeze, no crackles. No edema. Feet: intact skin, monofilament normal, pulses present.

A/P:
- AKI on CKD 3b: resolved; today's CMP to confirm creatinine back near 1.9.
- DM2 with nephropathy: A1c, UACR today. Metformin 500 BID.
- HTN on amlodipine 5: at goal.
- PAD: aspirin, atorvastatin; lipid panel.
- Lung cancer on surveillance, severe COPD on O2: per oncology; oxygen unchanged.
- Flu and COVID vaccines this fall.
Next visit booked 10/22. Missed the AWV in June because of the admission; will fold it into the fall visit.

documents.title: Your July labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hello Edward, your results from Monday are all back. Kidney function has come back to where it was before the hospital stay. A1c is steady and the urine protein is about the same as last year. Cholesterol remains well controlled. Blood counts are normal. Nothing to change. Enjoy the rest of the summer.

documents.title: RE: Your July labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks doc. Good to hear. Ed

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Optometry, exam 7/28/2026. Dilated fundus exam both eyes. Best corrected 20/25 right, 20/25 left. No diabetic retinopathy, no macular edema. Recheck in one year. Allergies on file: sulfa, iodinated contrast.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy fax for metformin 500 mg and amlodipine 5 mg, 90-day supply each. Seen 7/20 with labs. Approved per refill protocol, 90 days x1 refill. Pharmacy notified electronically.
